Primary Research Papers

PUBLISHED RESULTarXiv:2412.06769 (ICLR 2025)

Training Large Language Models to Reason in a Continuous Latent Space

2024Formal/Theoreticallatent-reasoning

LLMs can reason in continuous latent space by feeding the last hidden state directly as the next input embedding ("continuous thought"), enabling BFS-like search over reasoning paths rather than committing to a single deterministic trajectory as in language-space CoT.

Key Results
ProsQA accuracy (GPT-2)67.8%(Coconut (k=4))
ProsQA accuracy (GPT-2)54.2%(CoT baseline)
GSM8K (Llama 3.2-3B)31.7%(Coconut)
Paper Code
Limitations & What It Does NOT Demonstrate

Limitations:

• Training instability when adding multiple continuous thoughts at once

• Larger models show smaller gains due to extensive language pre-training

• Requires specialized multi-stage training curriculum

• Latent thoughts harder to interpret than language CoT

Does NOT demonstrate:

• Does not show latent reasoning works at scale without language pre-training

• Does not prove continuous thoughts are universally better than CoT

• No evaluation on open-ended generation tasks

PUBLISHED RESULTNeurIPS 2025

Scaling up Test-Time Compute with Latent Reasoning: A Recurrent Depth Approach

2025Experimentallatent-reasoning

A depth-recurrent transformer architecture can scale test-time compute by iterating a recurrent block in latent space, improving reasoning performance without generating additional tokens. Supports adaptive compute, KV-cache sharing, and speculative decoding.

Key Results
ARC-Challenge (3.5B)42.3%(r=32 recurrence)
ARC-Challenge (3.5B)34.1%(r=1 (baseline))
GSM8K (3.5B)58.7%(r=32 recurrence)
Paper Code
Limitations & What It Does NOT Demonstrate

Limitations:

• Not currently the dominant paradigm for reasoning

• Oversight concerns vs verbalized chain-of-thought

• Path independence and convergence behaviors need more study

• Requires training with random recurrence depth

Does NOT demonstrate:

• Does not surpass largest CoT models on all benchmarks

• Does not prove latent reasoning is always more compute-efficient

• Limited evaluation on very long-context tasks

PUBLISHED RESULTarXiv:2510.04871

Less is More: Recursive Reasoning with Tiny Networks

2025Experimentallatent-reasoning

Tiny Recursive Model (TRM) with a single 2-layer network (7M params) achieves 45% ARC-AGI-1 and 8% ARC-AGI-2, outperforming HRM and most LLMs with <0.01% parameters. Recursive refinement in latent space enables strong reasoning in tiny networks.

Key Results
ARC-AGI-1 test accuracy45%(TRM (7M params))
ARC-AGI-1 test accuracy40%(HRM (27M params))
ARC-AGI-2 test accuracy8%(TRM)
Paper
Limitations & What It Does NOT Demonstrate

Limitations:

• Optimal recursion depth exists (T=3,n=6 for TRM); more causes OOM

• Task-specific architectures needed

• Why recursion helps so much remains an open question

• EMA required for training stability

Does NOT demonstrate:

• Does not show TRM works on language modeling tasks

• Does not compare to HRM with matched compute budget

• No evaluation on non-puzzle reasoning tasks

PUBLISHED RESULTarXiv:2509.26507

The Dragon Hatchling: The Missing Link between the Transformer and Models of the Brain

2025Formal/Theoreticalbdh

BDH is a post-Transformer architecture based on scale-free biologically inspired network of n locally-interacting neuron particles. Couples theoretical foundations and interpretability with Transformer-like performance. Attention emerges from local graph dynamics at neurons and synapses ("Equations of Reasoning").

Key Results
Language modeling perplexityMatches GPT-2 scaling(BDH-GPU 10M-1B params)
Synaptic sparsity~5% active(Trained models)
Modularity emergenceScale-free graph structure(Learned connectivity)
Paper Code
Limitations & What It Does NOT Demonstrate

Limitations:

• Early stage; needs more real-world testing

• Sudoku results from internal implementation not open-source repo

• GPU-friendly formulation approximates idealized graph dynamics

• Long-context behavior vs KV-cache not fully characterized

Does NOT demonstrate:

• Does not yet surpass Transformers on all language benchmarks

• Does not prove brain-like architecture is necessary for reasoning

• Independent replication of scaling laws pending

PUBLISHED RESULTarXiv:2608.09888

BDH-CQ: In-Context Learning with Recurrent Latent Reasoning

2026Experimentalbdh-cq

BDH-CQ combines in-context learning with recurrent latent reasoning. Demonstrations update recurrent memory sequentially; query solved through iterative latent computation without verbalizing intermediate reasoning. 150M params reaches 29.5% ARC-AGI-1 pass@2 at $0.0007/task.

Key Results
ARC-AGI-1 public evaluation (pass@2)29.5%(BDH-CQ 150M)
ARC-AGI-1 cost per task$0.00070(H200 @ $3/hr)
ConceptARC dense mappingsStrong extrapolation(Propagation, copying tasks)
Paper
Limitations & What It Does NOT Demonstrate

Limitations:

• Ordering, nesting, conditional rule selection remain difficult

• Unseen parameter values and composition are failure modes

• Controlled experiments show specific concept-dependent gaps

• Visual reasoning only; language reasoning not evaluated

Does NOT demonstrate:

• Does not achieve SOTA accuracy on ARC (trades accuracy for cost)

• Does not show generalization beyond ARC-like visual tasks

• Does not evaluate on standard language benchmarks

2026Explanatorybdh

Transformer limitations (growing KV cache, dense computation, static weights) motivate brain-inspired design: neurons as computational units, synapses as memory, local computation, scale-free connectivity, and GPU-friendly implementation.

Paper

Does NOT demonstrate:

PUBLISHED RESULTPathway Research Blog

From Attention to Synapses: Deriving BDH

2026Formal/Theoreticalbdh

BDH architecture derived mathematically from attention equations: attention reorganized as synaptic memory in high-dimensional sparse neuron space with Hebbian updates and low-rank factorization leading to practical BDH-GPU.

Paper
Limitations & What It Does NOT Demonstrate

Limitations:

• Mathematical derivation; empirical validation in BDH paper

Does NOT demonstrate:

• Not independent experimental evidence

Evidence Discipline: How We Label Results

Every result in this lab is explicitly classified. Look for badges like these:

LIVE TOY COMPUTATIONPUBLISHED RESULTTOY / PEDAGOGICALILLUSTRATIVE DIAGRAM
  • LIVE TOY COMPUTATION — Runs in your browser right now (deterministic, seeded)
  • PUBLISHED RESULT — Directly from cited paper (with citation)
  • PRECOMPUTED RESULT — Precomputed from toy runs, saved as fixture
  • TOY / PEDAGOGICAL — Simplified simulation for teaching
  • ILLUSTRATIVE DIAGRAM — Conceptual visualization, not computation
  • REPORTED BY AUTHORS — Claim from paper, not independently verified

We never: make toy animations look like real model traces, merge benchmark data with toy results, or present developer benchmarks as independent evaluations.
